1.mohsin_khan: The Reality (i.e. the Day of Resurrection)!

3.sahih_international: And what can make you know what is the Inevitable Reality?
3.pickthall: Ah, what will convey unto thee what the reality is!
3.yusuf_ali: And what will make thee realise what the Sure Reality is?
3.shakir: And what would make you realize what the sure calamity is!
3.muhammad_sarwar: Would that you knew (in detail) what the Inevitable is!
3.mohsin_khan: And what will make you know what the Reality is?
3.arberry: And what will teach thee what is the Indubitable?

4.sahih_international: Thamud and 'Aad denied the Striking Calamity.
4.pickthall: (The tribes of) Thamud and A'ad disbelieved in the judgment to come.
4.yusuf_ali: The Thamud and the 'Ad People (branded) as false the Stunning Calamity!
4.shakir: Samood and Ad called the striking calamity a lie.
4.muhammad_sarwar: The people of Thamud and Ad denied the Day of Judgment.
4.mohsin_khan: Thamud and 'Ad people denied the Qari'ah [the striking Hour (of Judgement)]!
4.arberry: Thamood and Ad cried lies to the Clatterer.

5.sahih_international: So as for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overpowering [blast].
5.pickthall: As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the lightning.
5.yusuf_ali: But the Thamud,- they were destroyed by a terrible Storm of thunder and lightning!
5.shakir: Then as to Samood, they were destroyed by an excessively severe punishment.
5.muhammad_sarwar: The Thamuds were destroyed by a violent blast of sound.
5.mohsin_khan: As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the awful cry!
5.arberry: As for Thamood, they were destroyed by the Screamer;

6.sahih_international: And as for 'Aad, they were destroyed by a screaming, violent wind
6.pickthall: And as for A'ad, they were destroyed by a fierce roaring wind,
6.yusuf_ali: And the 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious Wind, exceedingly violent;
6.shakir: And as to Ad, they were destroyed by a roaring, violent blast.
6.muhammad_sarwar: The Ads were destroyed by a swift, destructive gale
6.mohsin_khan: And as for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious violent wind;
6.arberry: and as for Ad, they were destroyed by a wind clamorous,

7.sahih_international: Which Allah imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people therein fallen as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees.
7.pickthall: Which He imposed on them for seven long nights and eight long days so that thou mightest have seen men lying overthrown, as they were hollow trunks of palm-trees.
7.yusuf_ali: He made it rage against them seven nights and eight days in succession: so that thou couldst see the (whole) people lying prostrate in its (path), as they had been roots of hollow palm-trees tumbled down!
7.shakir: Which He made to prevail against them for seven nights and eight days unremittingly, so that you might have seen the people therein prostrate as if they were the trunks of hollow palms.
7.muhammad_sarwar: which continued to strike them for seven and eight days so that eventually you could see the people lying dead like the hollow trunks of uprooted palm-trees.
7.mohsin_khan: Which Allah imposed on them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so that you could see men lying overthrown (destroyed), as if they were hollow trunks of date-palms!
7.arberry: violent that He compelled against them seven nights and eight days, uninterruptedly, and thou mightest see the people laid prostrate in it as if they were the stumps of fallen down palm-trees.

8.sahih_international: Then do you see of them any remains?
8.pickthall: Canst thou (O Muhammad) see any remnant of them?
8.yusuf_ali: Then seest thou any of them left surviving?
8.shakir: Do you then see of them one remaining?
8.muhammad_sarwar: Can you see any of their survivors?
8.mohsin_khan: Do you see any remnants of them?
8.arberry: Now dost thou see any remnant of them?

9.sahih_international: And there came Pharaoh and those before him and the overturned cities with sin.
9.pickthall: And Pharaoh and those before him, and the communities that were destroyed, brought error,
9.yusuf_ali: And Pharaoh, and those before him, and the Cities Overthrown, committed habitual Sin.
9.shakir: And Firon and those before him and the overthrown cities continuously committed sins.
9.muhammad_sarwar: The Pharaoh, those who lived before him and the people of the Subverted Cities all persisted in doing evil.
9.mohsin_khan: And Fir'aun (Pharaoh), and those before him, and the cities overthrown [the towns of the people of [Lout (Lot)] committed sin,
9.arberry: Pharaoh likewise, and those before him, and the Subverted Cities -- they committed error,

10.sahih_international: And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a seizure exceeding [in severity].
10.pickthall: And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, therefor did He grip them with a tightening grip.
10.yusuf_ali: And disobeyed (each) the messenger of their Lord; so He punished them with an abundant Penalty.
10.shakir: And they disobeyed the Apostle of their Lord, so He punished them with a vehement punishment.
10.muhammad_sarwar: They disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord and He seized them with torment which increased with time.
10.mohsin_khan: And they disobeyed their Lord's Messenger, so He punished them with a strong punishment.
10.arberry: and they rebelled against the Messenger of their Lord, and He seized them with a surpassing grip.

11.sahih_international: Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried your ancestors in the sailing ship
11.pickthall: Lo! when the waters rose, We carried you upon the ship
11.yusuf_ali: We, when the water (of Noah's Flood) overflowed beyond its limits, carried you (mankind), in the floating (Ark),
11.shakir: Surely We bore you up in the ship when the water rose high,
11.muhammad_sarwar: When the flood rose high and covered the whole land, We carried you in the Ark.
11.mohsin_khan: Verily! When the water rose beyond its limits [Nuh's (Noah) Flood], We carried you (mankind) in the floating [ship that was constructed by Nuh (Noah)].
11.arberry: Lo, when the waters rose, We bore you in the running ship

12.sahih_international: That We might make it for you a reminder and [that] a conscious ear would be conscious of it.
12.pickthall: That We might make it a memorial for you, and that remembering ears (that heard the story) might remember.
12.yusuf_ali: That We might make it a Message unto you, and that ears (that should hear the tale and) retain its memory should bear its (lessons) in remembrance.
12.shakir: So that We may make it a reminder to you, and that the retaining ear might retain it.
12.muhammad_sarwar: as a lesson for you, but only attentive ears will retain it.
12.mohsin_khan: That We might make it a remembrance for you, and the keen ear (person) may (hear and) understand it.
12.arberry: that We might make it a reminder for you and for heeding ears to hold.

13.sahih_international: Then when the Horn is blown with one blast
13.pickthall: And when the trumpet shall sound one blast
13.yusuf_ali: Then, when one blast is sounded on the Trumpet,
13.shakir: And when the trumpet is blown with a single blast,
13.muhammad_sarwar: With the first blast of sound from the trumpet,
13.mohsin_khan: Then when the Trumpet will be blown with one blowing (the first one),
13.arberry: So, when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast

14.sahih_international: And the earth and the mountains are lifted and leveled with one blow -
14.pickthall: And the earth with the mountains shall be lifted up and crushed with one crash,
14.yusuf_ali: And the earth is moved, and its mountains, and they are crushed to powder at one stroke,-
14.shakir: And the earth and the mountains are borne away and crushed with a single crushing.
14.muhammad_sarwar: the earth and mountains will be raised up high and crushed all together.
14.mohsin_khan: And the earth and the mountains shall be removed from their places, and crushed with a single crushing,
14.arberry: and the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with a single blow,

15.sahih_international: Then on that Day, the Resurrection will occur,
15.pickthall: Then, on that day will the Event befall.
15.yusuf_ali: On that Day shall the (Great) Event come to pass.
15.shakir: On that day shall the great event come to pass,
15.muhammad_sarwar: On that day, the inevitable event will take place
15.mohsin_khan: Then on that Day shall the (Great) Event befall,
15.arberry: then, on that day, the Terror shall come to pass,

16.sahih_international: And the heaven will split [open], for that Day it is infirm.
16.pickthall: And the heaven will split asunder, for that day it will be frail.
16.yusuf_ali: And the sky will be rent asunder, for it will that Day be flimsy,
16.shakir: And the heaven shall cleave asunder, so that on that day it shall be frail,
16.muhammad_sarwar: and the heavens will be rent asunder,
16.mohsin_khan: And the heaven will split asunder, for that Day it (the heaven will be frail (weak), and torn up,
16.arberry: and heaven shall be split, for upon that day it shall be very frail,

17.sahih_international: And the angels are at its edges. And there will bear the Throne of your Lord above them, that Day, eight [of them].
17.pickthall: And the angels will be on the sides thereof, and eight will uphold the Throne of thy Lord that day, above them.
17.yusuf_ali: And the angels will be on its sides, and eight will, that Day, bear the Throne of thy Lord above them.
17.shakir: And the angels shall be on the sides thereof; and above them eight shall bear on that day your Lord's power.
17.muhammad_sarwar: and will turn frail, losing all force. The angels will be around the heavens and on that day eight of them will carry the Throne of your Lord above all the creatures.
17.mohsin_khan: And the angels will be on its sides, and eight angels will, that Day, bear the Throne of your Lord above them.
17.arberry: and the angels shall stand upon its borders, and upon that day eight shall carry above them the Throne of thy Lord.

18.sahih_international: That Day, you will be exhibited [for judgement]; not hidden among you is anything concealed.
18.pickthall: On that day ye will be exposed; not a secret of you will be hidden.
18.yusuf_ali: That Day shall ye be brought to Judgment: not an act of yours that ye hide will be hidden.
18.shakir: On that day you shall be exposed to view-- no secret of yours shall remain hidden.
18.muhammad_sarwar: On that day all your secrets will be exposed.
18.mohsin_khan: That Day shall you be brought to Judgement, not a secret of you will be hidden.
18.arberry: On that day you shall be exposed, not one secret of yours concealed.

19.sahih_international: So as for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, "Here, read my record!
19.pickthall: Then, as for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: Take, read my book!
19.yusuf_ali: Then he that will be given his Record in his right hand will say: "Ah here! Read ye my Record!
19.shakir: Then as for him who is given his book in his right hand, he will say: Lo! read my book:
19.muhammad_sarwar: Those who will receive the books of the records of their deeds in their right hands will say, "Come and read my record.
19.mohsin_khan: Then as for him who will be given his Record in his right hand will say: "Take, read my Record!
19.arberry: Then as for him who is given his book in his right hand, he shall say, 'Here, take and read my book!

20.sahih_international: Indeed, I was certain that I would be meeting my account."
20.pickthall: Surely I knew that I should have to meet my reckoning.
20.yusuf_ali: "I did really understand that my Account would (One Day) reach me!"
20.shakir: Surely I knew that I shall meet my account.
20.muhammad_sarwar: I was sure that the record of my deeds would be shown to me".
20.mohsin_khan: "Surely, I did believe that I shall meet my Account!"
20.arberry: Certainly I thought that I should encounter my reckoning.'

21.sahih_international: So he will be in a pleasant life -
21.pickthall: Then he will be in blissful state
21.yusuf_ali: And he will be in a life of Bliss,
21.shakir: So he shall be in a life of pleasure,
21.muhammad_sarwar: They will have a pleasant life
21.mohsin_khan: So he shall be in a life, well-pleasing.
21.arberry: So he shall be in a pleasing life

23.sahih_international: Its [fruit] to be picked hanging near.
23.pickthall: Whereof the clusters are in easy reach.
23.yusuf_ali: The Fruits whereof (will hang in bunches) low and near.
23.shakir: The fruits of which are near at hand:
23.mohsin_khan: The fruits in bunches whereof will be low and near at hand.

24.sahih_international: [They will be told], "Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you put forth in the days past."
24.pickthall: (And it will be said unto those therein): Eat and drink at ease for that which ye sent on before you in past days.
24.yusuf_ali: "Eat ye and drink ye, with full satisfaction; because of the (good) that ye sent before you, in the days that are gone!"
24.shakir: Eat and drink pleasantly for what you did beforehand in the days gone by.
24.muhammad_sarwar: Such people will be told, "Eat and drink with pleasure as the reward for what you did in the past".
24.mohsin_khan: Eat and drink at ease for that which you have sent on before you in days past!
24.arberry: 'Eat and drink with wholesome appetite for that you did long ago, in the days gone by.'

25.sahih_international: But as for he who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record
25.pickthall: But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say: Oh, would that I had not been given my book
25.yusuf_ali: And he that will be given his Record in his left hand, will say: "Ah! Would that my Record had not been given to me!
25.shakir: And as for him who is given his book in his left hand he shall say: O would that my book had never been given me:
25.muhammad_sarwar: However, those who will receive the books of the records of their deeds in their left hands will say, "We wish that this record had never been given to us
25.mohsin_khan: But as for him who will be given his Record in his left hand, will say: "I wish that I had not been given my Record!
25.arberry: But as for him who is given his book in his left hand, he shall say, 'Would that I had not been given my book

26.sahih_international: And had not known what is my account.
26.pickthall: And knew not what my reckoning!
26.yusuf_ali: "And that I had never realised how my account (stood)!
26.shakir: And I had not known what my account was:
26.muhammad_sarwar: and that we would never knew what our records contained.
26.mohsin_khan: "And that I had never known, how my Account is?

27.sahih_international: I wish my death had been the decisive one.
27.pickthall: Oh, would that it had been death!
27.yusuf_ali: "Ah! Would that (Death) had made an end of me!
27.shakir: O would that it had made an end (of me):
27.muhammad_sarwar: Would that death had taken us away for good.
27.mohsin_khan: "I wish, would that it had been my end (death)!
27.arberry: Would it had been the end!

28.sahih_international: My wealth has not availed me.
28.pickthall: My wealth hath not availed me,
28.yusuf_ali: "Of no profit to me has been my wealth!
28.shakir: My wealth has availed me nothing:
28.muhammad_sarwar: Our wealth is of no benefit to us
28.arberry: My wealth has not availed me,

29.sahih_international: Gone from me is my authority."
29.pickthall: My power hath gone from me.
29.shakir: My authority is gone away from me.
29.muhammad_sarwar: and our belief has destroyed us".
29.mohsin_khan: "My power and arguments (to defend myself) have gone from me!"
29.arberry: my authority is gone from me.'

30.sahih_international: [Allah will say], "Seize him and shackle him.
30.pickthall: (It will be said): Take him and fetter him
30.yusuf_ali: (The stern command will say): "Seize ye him, and bind ye him,
30.shakir: Lay hold on him, then put a chain on him,
30.muhammad_sarwar: The angels will be told, "Seize and chain them,
30.mohsin_khan: (It will be said): "Seize him and fetter him,

31.pickthall: And then expose him to hell-fire
31.yusuf_ali: "And burn ye him in the Blazing Fire.
31.shakir: Then cast him into the burning fire,
31.muhammad_sarwar: then throw them into hell to be heated up therein.
31.mohsin_khan: Then throw him in the blazing Fire.
31.arberry: and then roast him in Hell,

32.sahih_international: Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits insert him."
32.pickthall: And then insert him in a chain whereof the length is seventy cubits.
32.yusuf_ali: "Further, make him march in a chain, whereof the length is seventy cubits!
32.shakir: Then thrust him into a chain the length of which is seventy cubits.
32.muhammad_sarwar: Fasten a chain to them - seventy cubits long -
32.mohsin_khan: "Then fasten him with a chain whereof the length is seventy cubits!"
32.arberry: then in a chain of seventy cubits' length insert him!

33.sahih_international: Indeed, he did not used to believe in Allah, the Most Great,
33.pickthall: Lo! He used not to believe in Allah the Tremendous,
33.yusuf_ali: "This was he that would not believe in Allah Most High.
33.shakir: Surely he did not believe in Allah, the Great,
33.muhammad_sarwar: they did not believe in the great God,
33.mohsin_khan: Verily, He used not to believe in Allah, the Most Great,
33.arberry: Behold, he never believed in God the All-mighty,

34.sahih_international: Nor did he encourage the feeding of the poor.
34.pickthall: And urged not on the feeding of the wretched.
34.yusuf_ali: "And would not encourage the feeding of the indigent!
34.shakir: Nor did he urge the feeding of the poor.
34.muhammad_sarwar: nor were they concerned with feeding the destitute.
34.mohsin_khan: And urged not on the feeding of Al-Miskin (the poor),
34.arberry: and he never urged the feeding of the needy;

35.sahih_international: So there is not for him here this Day any devoted friend
35.pickthall: Therefor hath he no lover here this day,
35.yusuf_ali: "So no friend hath he here this Day.
35.shakir: Therefore he has not here today a true friend,
35.muhammad_sarwar: On this day, they will have no friends
35.mohsin_khan: So no friend has he here this Day,
35.arberry: therefore he today has not here one loyal friend,

36.sahih_international: Nor any food except from the discharge of wounds;
36.yusuf_ali: "Nor hath he any food except the corruption from the washing of wounds,
36.mohsin_khan: Nor any food except filth from the washing of wounds,
36.arberry: neither any food saving foul pus,

37.sahih_international: None will eat it except the sinners.
37.yusuf_ali: "Which none do eat but those in sin."
37.shakir: Which none but the wrongdoers eat.
37.mohsin_khan: None will eat except the Khati'un (sinners, disbelievers, polytheists, etc.).
37.arberry: that none excepting the sinners eat.'

38.sahih_international: So I swear by what you see
38.pickthall: But nay! I swear by all that ye see
38.yusuf_ali: So I do call to witness what ye see,
38.shakir: But nay! I swear by that which you see,
38.muhammad_sarwar: I do not need to swear by what you see
38.mohsin_khan: So I swear by whatsoever you see,
38.arberry: No! I swear by that you see

39.sahih_international: And what you do not see
39.pickthall: And all that ye see not
39.shakir: And that which you do not see.
39.muhammad_sarwar: and what you do not see
39.mohsin_khan: And by whatsoever you see not,
39.arberry: and by that you do not see,

40.sahih_international: [That] indeed, the Qur'an is the word of a noble Messenger.
40.pickthall: That it is indeed the speech of an illustrious messenger.
40.yusuf_ali: That this is verily the word of an honoured messenger;
40.shakir: Most surely, it is the Word brought by an honored Apostle,
40.muhammad_sarwar: because the Quran is certainly the word of a reverent messenger.
40.mohsin_khan: That this is verily the word of an honoured Messenger [i.e. Jibrael (Gabriel) or Muhammad SAW which he has brought from Allah].
40.arberry: it is the speech of a noble Messenger.

41.sahih_international: And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe.
41.pickthall: It is not poet's speech - little is it that ye believe!
41.yusuf_ali: It is not the word of a poet: little it is ye believe!
41.shakir: And it is not the word of a poet; little is it that you believe;
41.muhammad_sarwar: It is not the word of a poet but only a few of you have faith,
41.mohsin_khan: It is not the word of a poet, little is that you believe!
41.arberry: It is not the speech of a poet (little do you believe)

42.sahih_international: Nor the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember.
42.pickthall: Nor diviner's speech - little is it that ye remember!
42.yusuf_ali: Nor is it the word of a soothsayer: little admonition it is ye receive.
42.shakir: Nor the word of a soothsayer; little is it that you mind.
42.muhammad_sarwar: nor is it the work of a soothsayer but only a few of you take heed.
42.mohsin_khan: Nor is it the word of a soothsayer (or a foreteller), little is that you remember!
42.arberry: nor the speech of a soothsayer (little do you remember).

43.sahih_international: [It is] a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
43.pickthall: It is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds.
43.yusuf_ali: (This is) a Message sent down from the Lord of the Worlds.
43.shakir: It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
43.muhammad_sarwar: It is a revelation from the Lord of the Universe.
43.mohsin_khan: This is the Revelation sent down from the Lord of the 'Alamin (mankind, jinns and all that exists).
43.arberry: A sending down from the Lord of all Being.

44.sahih_international: And if Muhammad had made up about Us some [false] sayings,
44.pickthall: And if he had invented false sayings concerning Us,
44.yusuf_ali: And if the messenger were to invent any sayings in Our name,
44.shakir: And if he had fabricated against Us some of the sayings,
44.muhammad_sarwar: Had Muhammad invented some words against Us,.
44.mohsin_khan: And if he (Muhammad SAW) had forged a false saying concerning Us (Allah),
44.arberry: Had he invented against Us any sayings,

45.sahih_international: We would have seized him by the right hand;
45.pickthall: We assuredly had taken him by the right hand
45.yusuf_ali: We should certainly seize him by his right hand,
45.shakir: We would certainly have seized him by the right hand,
45.muhammad_sarwar: We would have caught hold of him by his right hand
45.mohsin_khan: We surely should have seized him by his right hand (or with power and might),
45.arberry: We would have seized him by the right hand,

46.sahih_international: Then We would have cut from him the aorta.
46.yusuf_ali: And We should certainly then cut off the artery of his heart:
46.shakir: Then We would certainly have cut off his aorta.
46.mohsin_khan: And then certainly should have cut off his life artery (Aorta),
46.arberry: then We would surely have cut his life-vein

47.sahih_international: And there is no one of you who could prevent [Us] from him.
47.pickthall: And not one of you could have held Us off from him.
47.yusuf_ali: Nor could any of you withhold him (from Our wrath).
47.shakir: And not one of you could have withheld Us from him.
47.muhammad_sarwar: None of you would be able to prevent Us from doing this to him.
47.mohsin_khan: And none of you could withhold Us from (punishing) him.
47.arberry: and not one of you could have defended him.

48.sahih_international: And indeed, the Qur'an is a reminder for the righteous.
48.pickthall: And lo! it is a warrant unto those who ward off (evil).
48.yusuf_ali: But verily this is a Message for the Allah-fearing.
48.shakir: And most surely it is a reminder for those who guard (against evil).
48.muhammad_sarwar: The Quran is certainly a reminder for the pious ones.
48.mohsin_khan: And verily, this Quran is a Reminder for the Muttaqun (pious - see V. 2:2).
48.arberry: Surely it is a Reminder to the godfearing;

49.sahih_international: And indeed, We know that among you are deniers.
49.pickthall: And lo! We know that some among you will deny (it).
49.yusuf_ali: And We certainly know that there are amongst you those that reject (it).
49.shakir: And most surely We know that some of you are rejecters.
49.muhammad_sarwar: We certainly know that some of you have rejected it
49.mohsin_khan: And verily, We know that there are some among you that belie (this Quran). [Tafsir At-Tabari, Vol. 29, Page 68]
49.arberry: but We know that some of you will cry lies.

50.sahih_international: And indeed, it will be [a cause of] regret upon the disbelievers.
50.pickthall: And lo! it is indeed an anguish for the disbelievers.
50.yusuf_ali: But truly (Revelation) is a cause of sorrow for the Unbelievers.
50.shakir: And most surely it is a great grief to the unbelievers.
50.muhammad_sarwar: and (on the Day of Judgment) this will be a great source of regret for the unbelievers.
50.mohsin_khan: And indeed it (this Quran) will be an anguish for the disbelievers (on the Day of Resurrection).
50.arberry: Surely it is a sorrow to the unbelievers;

51.sahih_international: And indeed, it is the truth of certainty.
51.pickthall: And lo! it is absolute truth.
51.yusuf_ali: But verily it is Truth of assured certainty.
51.shakir: And most surely it is the true certainty
51.muhammad_sarwar: This is the Truth beyond any doubt.
51.mohsin_khan: And Verily, it (this Quran) is an absolute truth with certainty.
51.arberry: yet indeed it is the truth of certainty.

52.sahih_international: So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great.
52.pickthall: So glorify the name of thy Tremendous Lord.
52.yusuf_ali: So glorify the name of thy Lord Most High.
52.shakir: Therefore-glorify the name of your Lord, the Great.
52.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), glorify the name of your Lord, the Great One.
52.mohsin_khan: So glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most Great.
52.arberry: Then magnify the Name of thy Lord, the All-mighty.
